concepts.def: The roughly 24-hour period for the Sun to return to the same position in the sky, the basis of civil clock time.
The roughly 23 hours 56 minutes for the Earth to rotate once relative to the distant stars, slightly shorter than the solar day.
The roughly 365.24 days for the seasons to repeat, which is why a leap day is added about every four years to keep the calendar aligned.
A year with an extra day (29 February) so the calendar's average length matches the tropical year; years divisible by 4 are leap years, with century exceptions.
A region using a common standard time, usually offset by whole hours from Greenwich Mean Time, so local noon roughly matches the Sun's highest point.
The difference between a sundial's apparent solar time and a clock's mean solar time, caused by Earth's axial tilt and elliptical orbit.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Time & the Calendar — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Time & the Calendar brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Time & the Calendar.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why is a sidereal day shorter than a solar day?
options: Earth speeds up at night
Earth must turn a little extra to face the Sun again
The stars move quickly
Clocks are simply wrong

mcqs.q: A leap day is added because the tropical year is about:
options: Exactly 365 days
365.24 days
366 days
360 days

mcqs.q: Time zones are measured relative to:
options: The Equator
Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)
The Moon
Local sunrise

mcqs.q: Why do we add a leap day every four years?
options: The Sun switching off and on.
Because the Earth slows down each year.
Because the year is about 365.24 days, so an extra day keeps the calendar aligned.
To make February longer for no reason.

mcqs.q: Is a sidereal day the same as a solar day?
options: A sidereal day is exactly twice as long.
The Sun switching off and on.
They are identical 24-hour periods.
No - a sidereal day (relative to the stars) is about four minutes shorter.
The Earth moving around the Sun.
A sidereal day is exactly twice as long.
The Sun switching off and on.
The Earth rotating on its axis.
